challengeTypes: identify: On a number line, which number is to the LEFT of zero? (-3 vs 3 vs 0 vs 1)

sort: Drag each real-life situation to positive or negative (Mountain peak 1000m above sea level = +1000 | Submarine 200m below sea level = -200 | Temperature 5 degrees above zero = +5 | Temperature 3 degrees below zero = -3 | Bank deposit 500 = +500 | Bank withdrawal 200 = -200)
identify: Which is greater: -5 or -1? (-1 vs -5 vs equal vs cannot compare)
sort: Drag each integer to its correct position on the number line (Smallest to Largest: -4, -1, 0, 2, 5)

extraInstructions: IMPORTANT: You MUST import and use BOTH audioManager AND speechManager. Import speechManager from '../../../lib/sim-engine/speech'. Use audioManager.play() for sound effects (valid: pickup, drop-correct, drop-wrong, tap, success, error, celebration, hint). Use speechManager.speak() for spoken teaching slide narration, challenge questions, correct/incorrect feedback, and hints. The game must teach: (1) Negative numbers — numbers less than zero, shown on the LEFT of zero on a number line. Real-life examples: temperature below zero, below sea level, bank debt. (2) Integers — the complete set: counting numbers (1,2,3...), zero (0), and negatives of counting numbers (-1,-2,-3...). Written as {..., -3, -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3, ...}. (3) Comparison of integers — any number to the RIGHT on the number line is GREATER. Any number to the LEFT is SMALLER. -5 is LESS than -1 because -5 is further left. 0 is greater than any negative number. (4) Ascending and descending order — ascending = smallest to largest (left to right on number line), descending = largest to smallest. Example: -3, -1, 0, 2, 5 (ascending). (5) Addition and subtraction rules — Same signs: add the numbers and keep the sign. -3 + (-2) = -5. Opposite signs: subtract the smaller from the larger and keep the sign of the larger. 3 + (-5) = -2 (5-3=2, sign of 5 is negative). Subtracting a negative = adding a positive: (-2) - (-4) = (-2) + 4 = 2. Misconceptions: '-5 is greater than -1 because 5 is bigger than 1' (WRONG — on a number line, -5 is further LEFT, so it is SMALLER), 'negative numbers do not exist' (WRONG — they represent real situations like debt, below-zero temperature, below sea level), 'adding two negatives gives a positive' (WRONG — same signs add and keep the sign, so -3 + (-2) = -5, not +5), 'subtracting a negative makes it more negative' (WRONG — subtracting a negative is the same as adding a positive, so 4 - (-2) = 4 + 2 = 6).
